issues.body:
## Why

Current break: `.gitignore:64` ignores every `*.csv`, while `tests/baseline/test_golden/test_baseline_derived_metrics.csv` is a versioned golden fixture. `git check-ignore -v tests/__audit_golden_probe__.csv` identifies `.gitignore:64` as the rule that ignores a new test CSV, so a newly created golden fixture can be absent from review and version control.

## Scope

Preserve the generated-output CSV ignore rule while exempting only the repository's versioned golden-fixture directory.

## Implementation Notes

Place a narrow negated ignore pattern after the broad CSV rule. Add a static test that checks a hypothetical fixture path so the test does not create or remove a file.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update `.gitignore` with a narrow exception for CSV files under `tests/baseline/test_golden/`.
- [ ] Add `tests/test_golden_csv_tracking.py` to verify that a hypothetical golden CSV path is not ignored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/test_golden_csv_tracking.py::test_golden_fixture_pattern_is_not_ignored` passes and the broad generated-output CSV rule remains in `.gitignore`.
- temporarily remove the golden-fixture exception and confirm tests/test_golden_csv_tracking.py::test_golden_fixture_pattern_is_not_ignored fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

- Do not unignore unrelated CSV outputs outside `tests/baseline/test_golden/`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding a test while new golden CSV fixtures remain ignored is a failure of this issue.
issues.title: [P2] Allow versioned golden CSV fixtures to be tracked

issues.body:
## Why

Current break: `src/trend_analysis/regimes.py:53-57` converts regime numbers without checking finiteness, while `src/trend_analysis/regimes.py:72, 91-103` applies Python `bool()` to configuration flags and stores unchecked threshold and neutral-band values. `src/trend_analysis/pipeline_helpers.py:281-294` can pass a NaN fund-count multiplier to `int(round(...))`; `src/trend_analysis/pipeline_helpers.py:344-360` can emit NaN or infinity target volatility. As a result, `enabled: "false"` enables the subsystem and supplied non-finite controls either crash later or reach portfolio calculations.

## Scope

Validate regime flags as booleans and validate supplied regime numeric controls as finite before regime classification and risk-off overrides consume them.

## Implementation Notes

Use one documented boolean coercion rule for YAML-compatible flag values. Reject non-finite supplied values rather than treating them as defaults, including risk-off count and target-volatility modifiers.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update `src/trend_analysis/regimes.py` to reject string boolean flags and non-finite regime threshold or neutral-band values.
- [ ] Update `src/trend_analysis/pipeline_helpers.py` to reject non-finite risk-off fund-count and target-volatility modifiers.
- [ ] Extend `tests/test_regime_annualise.py` with invalid boolean and non-finite base-control coverage.
- [ ] Extend `tests/test_pipeline_optional_features.py` with non-finite risk-off override coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/test_regime_annualise.py::test_regime_control_values_reject_non_finite_and_string_boolean tests/test_pipeline_optional_features.py::test_regime_overrides_reject_non_finite_modifiers` passes.
- temporarily remove the finite-value guard and confirm tests/test_regime_annualise.py::test_regime_control_values_reject_non_finite_and_string_boolean fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change regime-label selection semantics in `src/trend_analysis/regimes.py`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: accepting a string flag or non-finite modifier that reaches a regime calculation is a failure of this issue.
issues.title: [P2] Validate regime control booleans and finite numeric values

issues.body:
## Why

Current break: `src/trend_analysis/pipeline_helpers.py:231-240` raises `CoreConfigError` for an unrecognised regime cap key, and `tests/test_pipeline_helpers_additional.py:280-290` verifies that `mystery` is rejected. `src/trend_analysis/pipeline_runner.py:106-114` catches that error and substitutes `None`; `src/trend_analysis/risk.py:171-187` treats `None` as no cap. A misspelled configured regime can therefore produce an uncapped run.

## Scope

Preserve the parser's invalid-regime-cap error through the pipeline entrypoint and prevent execution with an omitted cap caused by that parsing failure.

## Implementation Notes

Let `CoreConfigError` surface as the established configuration failure type, or translate it once at the user-facing entrypoint. Do not conflate an invalid mapping with an absent `max_turnover` setting.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update `src/trend_analysis/pipeline_runner.py` to propagate an invalid regime turnover-cap parsing error instead of assigning `None`.
- [ ] Extend `tests/test_pipeline_entrypoints.py` with an end-to-end invalid `portfolio.max_turnover` regime-key case.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/test_pipeline_entrypoints.py::test_run_from_config_rejects_invalid_regime_turnover_cap` passes and observes the parser error before portfolio weighting.
- temporarily restore the CoreConfigError-to-None fallback and confirm tests/test_pipeline_entrypoints.py::test_run_from_config_rejects_invalid_regime_turnover_cap fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change the recognised regime-label aliases in `src/trend_analysis/pipeline_helpers.py`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: surfacing an error while still continuing with an uncapped portfolio is a failure of this issue.
issues.title: [P2] Fail closed when regime turnover-cap parsing fails

issues.body:
## Why

Current break: `src/trend_analysis/config/model.py:517-528` converts `portfolio.lambda_tc` with `float()` and checks only the numeric interval, so NaN passes both comparisons. `src/trend_analysis/risk.py:156-168` then uses that NaN in the turnover blend and returns NaN weights when previous weights are supplied. The fallback validator repeats the interval-only check at `src/trend_analysis/config/models.py:482-492`.

## Scope

Reject NaN and both infinities for `portfolio.lambda_tc` in every supported configuration validation path while preserving finite values in the inclusive `[0, 1]` interval.

## Implementation Notes

Perform the finite check after numeric coercion and before the existing bounds check. Keep the present null and blank-value behaviour unless a compatibility review identifies a required change.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update `src/trend_analysis/config/model.py` to reject non-finite `portfolio.lambda_tc` after coercion.
- [ ] Update `src/trend_analysis/config/models.py` to enforce the same rejection in runtime and fallback portfolio validation.
- [ ] Extend `tests/test_config_turnover_validation.py` with NaN and infinity coverage for `portfolio.lambda_tc`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/test_config_turnover_validation.py::test_lambda_tc_rejects_non_finite` passes while finite values from 0 through 1 remain accepted.
- temporarily remove the finite check and confirm tests/test_config_turnover_validation.py::test_lambda_tc_rejects_non_finite fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

- Do not alter the turnover-penalty formula in `src/trend_analysis/risk.py`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding coverage without rejecting non-finite values in both validation paths is a failure of this issue.
issues.title: [P2] Reject non-finite portfolio.lambda_tc values before weighting

## Why

`src/trend_analysis/config/model.py:658-665` rejects `signals.min_periods > signals.window` at config load, but `src/trend_analysis/signals.py:121-127` `TrendSpec.__post_init__` does not, and `tests/test_pipeline_helpers_additional.py:911-917` only guards `min_periods=0`. Runtime currently fails later with a pandas error message instead of the config-model contract.

## Scope

Add the same guard to `TrendSpec` and `pipeline_helpers.compute_signal`. Mirror tests from `tests/test_trend_config_model.py:140-148` for runtime entry points.

## Implementation Notes

- Reuse error text `signals.min_periods cannot exceed signals.window.` for consistency.
- `trend_spec_from_mapping` in `src/trend_analysis/signals.py:222-230` should inherit the guard via `TrendSpec`.
- Do not change preset clamping behaviour in `tests/test_presets_extended.py:47-49` unless presets rely on silent clamping (verify first).

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `min_periods <= window` validation to `TrendSpec.__post_init__` in `src/trend_analysis/signals.py`
- [ ] Add the same check to `compute_signal` in `src/trend_analysis/pipeline_helpers.py`
- [ ] Add `test_trend_spec_rejects_min_periods_above_window` in `tests/test_trend_signals_validation.py`
- [ ] Extend `test_compute_signal_error_paths` in `tests/test_pipeline_helpers_additional.py` for `min_periods > window`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/test_trend_config_model.py::test_signal_min_periods_cannot_exceed_window tests/test_trend_signals_validation.py tests/test_pipeline_helpers_additional.py::test_compute_signal_error_paths -q` passes
- [ ] `TrendSpec(window=5, min_periods=6)` raises `ValueError` before any pandas rolling call

## Non-Goals

- Changing `SignalSettings` pydantic model fields
- Altering default window/min_periods in shipped YAML configs

issues.body:
## Why

`src/trend_analysis/util/weights.py:35-40` only converts inputs when `sum(abs)` ≈ 100 or ≈ 1; otherwise weights pass through unchanged (e.g. `{A:30, B:20}` stays 30/20). Callers in `src/trend_analysis/api.py:340` and `src/trend_analysis/multi_period/engine.py:159` rely on this helper with no test for the ambiguous band in `tests/test_weights_utils.py`.

## Scope

Document and enforce the intended behaviour for totals that are neither percent-like nor fraction-like. Add boundary tests; adjust implementation only if product owner wants rejection or sum-normalisation (default: divide by `total_abs` when `total_abs > 0` and not close to 1 or 100).

## Implementation Notes

- Existing tests at `tests/test_weights_utils.py:9-33` cover percent and fraction paths.
- Preserve long-short percent case at `tests/test_weights_utils.py:43-47` (`120, -20` sums to 100).
- Add explicit tests for `sum=0`, ambiguous mid-range, and negative totals not summing to 100.
- Update docstring on `normalize_weights` to state the chosen rule.

## Tasks

- [ ] Decide and implement ambiguous-total handling in `src/trend_analysis/util/weights.py`
- [ ] Add boundary tests in `tests/test_weights_utils.py` for ambiguous and zero-sum inputs
- [ ] Verify `src/trend_analysis/api.py` callers still receive expected fractions in a smoke test if needed

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/test_weights_utils.py -q` passes
- [ ] new test `test_normalize_weights_ambiguous_total` documents the chosen rule with exact expected values
- [ ] temporarily remove ambiguous-total handling in `src/trend_analysis/util/weights.py` and confirm `test_normalize_weights_ambiguous_total` fails; revert

## Non-Goals

- Changing portfolio optimisation weight constraints in `src/trend_analysis/stages/portfolio.py`
- UI copy changes in Streamlit pages

Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a docstring-only change without a failing-before/passing-after test is a failure of this issue.

issues.body:
## Why

`src/trend_analysis/signals.py:3-5` states all execution paths use one signal implementation, but `src/trend_analysis/pipeline_helpers.py:550-601` implements a separate rolling-mean `compute_signal` with fixed `shift(1)`. Equivalence is tested only for `window=4, min_periods=4` in `tests/test_trend_signals.py:69-74`. This is a latent divergence risk between the legacy helper and the engine path.

## Scope

Make `pipeline.compute_signal` a thin delegate to `compute_trend_signals` (or remove the duplicate and update callers). Expand tests so lag and multi-column frames cannot drift silently.

## Implementation Notes

- Production portfolio stages already call `compute_trend_signals`; `compute_signal` is only exported from `src/trend_analysis/pipeline.py` for tests/scripts.
- Map parameters: `column` → single-column frame, `window`/`min_periods` → `TrendSpec`, honour `spec.lag` instead of hard-coded `shift(1)`.
- Keep the public `pipeline.compute_signal` signature stable for downstream test imports.
- Extend `tests/test_trend_signals.py` with at least one case where `lag=2` and multi-column input match between helpers.

## Tasks

- [ ] Refactor `src/trend_analysis/pipeline_helpers.py` `compute_signal` to delegate to `src/trend_analysis/signals.py` `compute_trend_signals`
- [ ] Update `src/trend_analysis/pipeline.py` wrapper if signature mapping changes
- [ ] Add lag/multi-column equivalence tests in `tests/test_trend_signals.py`
- [ ] Run `tests/test_shift_safe_pipeline.py` and fix any regressions from unified implementation

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/test_trend_signals.py tests/test_shift_safe_pipeline.py -q` passes
- [ ] `rg 'rolling.*mean.*shift\(1\)' src/trend_analysis/pipeline_helpers.py` no longer matches inside `compute_signal`
- [ ] temporarily change `TrendSpec.lag` default in `src/trend_analysis/signals.py` and confirm `tests/test_trend_signals.py::test_pipeline_compute_signal_uses_trend_engine` fails; revert

## Non-Goals

- Removing `compute_trend_signals` caching or vol-adjust/z-score behaviour
- Refactoring unrelated pipeline helper functions

Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a delegate that still duplicates rolling logic inline is a failure of this issue.
issues.title: [P2] Reconcile pipeline compute_signal with canonical compute_trend_signals

## Why

`tests/app/test_data_page.py:31`, `tests/app/test_results_page.py:20`, `tests/app/test_validation_page_renders.py:22`, and `tests/streamlit/test_mc_page.py:54` each define a separate `DummyStreamlit` class. This is a latent maintenance break: widget API drift in one page test will not fail the others until runtime.

## Scope

Create one shared Streamlit stub for unit tests and migrate the four page test modules to import it. Preserve existing assertion behaviour in each test file.

## Implementation Notes

- Place the canonical stub under `tests/support/dummy_streamlit.py` (or `tests/conftest.py` if the repo already centralises fixtures there).
- Merge capabilities from all four copies (column contexts, expanders, MC-specific widgets, session_state helpers).
- Keep page-specific `_load_page` / `data_page` fixtures local; only the stub class moves.
- Do not replace AppTest smoke tests in `tests/baseline/test_streamlit_smoke.py`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `tests/support/dummy_streamlit.py` with the merged `DummyStreamlit` implementation
- [ ] Update `tests/app/test_data_page.py` to import the shared stub
- [ ] Update `tests/app/test_results_page.py` to import the shared stub
- [ ] Update `tests/app/test_validation_page_renders.py` to import the shared stub

- Changing production `streamlit_app/` code
